newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Currency woes bedevil Singapore rubber trade.
newsitem.headline: Currency woes bedevil Singapore rubber trade.

text.p: The pounding taken by Southeast Asian currencies continued to hound the Singapore rubber trade on Friday with sellers from Indonesia scouring the market for buyers, dealers said.
"The Indonesians were very keen sellers today, but there were very few buyers. With all these currencies heading down, nobody wanted to buy," a dealer said.

The Indonesian unit plunged to a fresh low of around 2,915 rupiah to the U.S. dollar at around 0700 GMT from 2,770/90 at the opening. "The Indonesians wanted to unload material, but there was no one around to pick it up," another trader said.
Talk was also circulating in the market about the possibility Bangkok may be forced to sell some of its stocks soon as part of a rescue package with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"That kind of talk is going around the market and making some people nervous," a dealer said. Activity in the local exchange, however, was modest with some houses engaged in light bargain-hunting for low-priced rubber supplies.
At around 0945 GMT, Oct RSS3 was seen at 92.50 U.S. cents a kg from 93.00 cents.
